trigger: An exact technician workstation command fails, hangs, false-passes, or produces output inconsistent with repository contracts.
preconditions: The operator supplied the exact command, shell, output, and machine boundary.
The repository state can be preserved without reset, clean, overwrite, or force push.
The failure belongs to the technician live-cert or owned repair surface.

steps.action: Preserve the failed run directory and capture sanitized failure classification without committing private evidence. When failure occurs before repository identity is proven, preserve the shell output and run Test-Technician-Toolchain-Preflight.cmd before any fetch, pull, or worktree operation.
steps.output: failure boundary, run ID when available, command, shell, exit identity, evidence path

steps.action: Identify why existing tests allowed the defect: blocked or misresolved executable, skipped shell, static token-only check, tracked-but-unparsed PowerShell entrypoint, unexecuted report generator, unexecuted branch, overload ambiguity, path-resolution timing, pager interaction, or proof inflation. PATH/Get-Command presence alone is insufficient for an executable dependency; file existence and tracking alone are insufficient for a PowerShell harness entrypoint.
steps.output: harness-gap classification plus parser/execution failure evidence and toolchain-preflight JSON/Markdown when executable launch is implicated

steps.action: Repair the executable defect and add the smallest deterministic guard that would have failed before field use. For a harness reporter or validator, require PowerShell parser success and execute the reporter into an untracked temporary output root, proving both machine-readable and English report artifacts. Harness-only toolchain failures are repaired in validators, registries, workflows, hooks, skills, reports, or entrypoint wrappers without unrelated product mutation.
steps.output: tracked harness code plus validator or fixture

steps.action: Run the owning validators in Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7. The harness validator must parse every registered PowerShell harness entrypoint and execute the status reporter before success. Include bounded Windows toolchain launch proof when relevant, then run Python contracts and noninteractive Git hygiene.
steps.output: cross-shell validation ledger including status-reporter JSON and English Markdown generation proof

steps.action: Rerun the exact operator command on the affected workstation or a separately authorized equivalent machine only after the failing prerequisite is proven healthy.
steps.output: new run evidence at the next honest proof level

steps.action: Commit, push, open/update the PR, report the exact head, and provide an isolated-worktree command that preserves any local branch. If Git itself is blocked, provide a no-Git toolchain diagnostic command first rather than pretending fetch is executable.

stopConditions: The failure crosses into unowned product behavior.
The exact operator shell or machine boundary is unknown.
Windows cannot launch any concrete Git executable; repository synchronization remains blocked until that prerequisite is repaired.
Repair requires credentials, private evidence, destructive cleanup, merge, deployment, or live mutation without authority.
The candidate cannot be validated in every required shell.
proofCeiling: A repaired contract, parser/execution guard, and cross-shell CI do not prove the original workstation path until the exact operator command passes. A successful status-reporter smoke check proves harness report generation only. A successful toolchain preflight proves executable launch only, not fetch or runtime behavior.
